10.1002_adma.202523353: The electrochemical upgrading of glycerol into a single, valuable C 3 product remains a long‐standing challenge, constrained by the limitations of insufficient activity, low selectivity, and poor stability. Here, we report a ternary PdNiMo alloy catalyst that synergistically modulates the electronic structure and optimizes the surface *OH coverage for efficient and stable glycerol‐to‐glycerate conversion. Combined experimental and theoretical studies reveal that Mo incorporation downshifts the d‐band center and weakens *OH binding, while Ni introduction optimizes the balance between *OH‐covered and free Pd sites. The resulting PdNiMo catalyst exhibits exceptional GEOR performance, achieving a high current density of 171 mA cm −2 at 0.8 V vs. RHE and a superior glycerate selectivity of 67.5%. More impressively, in a membrane electrode assembly electrolyzer, the catalyst demonstrates outstanding durability, maintaining a current density of over 50 mA cm −2 for more than 1000 h at a cell voltage of 1.2 V cell . This work elucidates the critical role of tailored hydroxyl coverage in selective oxidation and provides a design principle for advanced electrocatalysts in renewable energy‐powered electrosynthesis.
10.1002_smll.76670: Quasi‐2D Ruddlesden–Popper (2DRP) perovskites offer improved environmental stability in relation to their 3D counterparts. However, their multiple‐quantum‐well structure and insulating organic spacers inherently limit vertical charge transport, significantly reducing device performance in scalable printed films. Herein, we employ methylammonium chloride (MACl) as a crystallization‐modulating additive to overcome these transport bottlenecks in ambient printed 2DRP perovskite solar cells (PSCs). Focusing on an n = 9 2DRP absorber, MACl modulates precursor interactions involving organic spacers and guides phase evolution during film formation. This modulation yields a highly uniform phase distribution dominated by large‐n 2DRP phases while enhancing crystallinity and vertical orientation. Consequently, trap‐mediated recombination is significantly suppressed, leading to enhanced carrier mobility and facilitating efficient photocurrent generation. As a result, the optimized 1 cm 2 printed 2DRP‐based PSC achieves a remarkable power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 14.4%, in relation to the negligible PCE (0.4%) of the control device. Furthermore, this strategy is successfully validated across various compositions ( n = 2, 4, 5, and 7), demonstrating a versatile and broadly applicable route for the development of high‐performance, scalable printed 2DRP‐based PSCs.
10.1016_j.est.2026.122730: The aim of this research is to develop a methodology, useful during real-world battery applications, for identifying aging phenomena for in-operando degradation estimation. In this way the state of health (SOH) of the cell is no longer intended as the simple residual capacity of the battery but is linked to physical and mechanical degradation. This new approach allows to valorise different aging profiles making a distinction between cells with the same SOH but different aging histories, thus opening the way for a modern battery diagnostics. The developed methodology intends to define an aging model for lithium-ion batteries with potential relevance to automotive Battery Management System (BMS), stationary Battery Energy Storage System (BESS), and second-life screening incorporating relevant features identified through differential voltage analysis (DVA). The developed model offers an accurate battery diagnostics providing the SOH and giving indications of the specific type of aging experienced by the cells. Experimental data coming from laboratory tests have been used to implement a code capable of processing charging curves at a standard rate of C/2, and returning battery SOH, loss of active material (LAM) and loss of lithium inventory (LLI) with a good accuracy when compared with C/20 reference curves. With an obtained main significant error (MSE) ranging between 0.2 and 2% the proposed method is sufficiently accurate for the purposes for which it is intended, and its implementation in real battery BMS boards could offer a solution for modern smart battery applications, improving the safety and efficiency of modern battery systems.
10.1016_j.microc.2026.118411: Sarcosine (N-methylglycine) has emerged as a promising biomarker for the early diagnosis of prostate cancer, allowing non-invasive detection in biological fluids and exhibiting greater specificity than PSA. This work, a molecularly imprinted polymer (MIP) selective for sarcosine was synthesized and applied to the extraction and detection of the analyte in aqueous medium, aiming at the development of a sensitive, selective, and low-cost analytical methodology. The MIP, obtained by block polymerization, was compared to the non-imprinted polymer (NIP) in terms of selectivity, adsorption capacity, kinetics, equilibrium isotherms, and reusability. The material showed a maximum adsorption capacity of 3.95 mg g-1, approximately three times higher than that of the NIP (1.35 mg g-1), following a pseudo-second-order kinetic model and fitting the Freundlich and Scatchard isotherms. MIP also demonstrated high selectivity towards structural analogs, with selectivity factors up to eight times higher than those obtained for NIP. Solid-phase pre-concentration using MIP allowed for selective enrichment of sarcosine, increasing analytical sensitivity approximately ninefold. Optimized elution with ACN/carbonate buffer (1:1, pH 10.5) resulted in detection and quantification limits of 0.060 and 0.019 mg L-1, respectively. The polymer showed excellent stability and reusability over ten consecutive cycles without significant loss of performance. The methodology was applied to samples of healthy prostate cells (PNT-2) and tumor cells (LNCaP), with fluorimetric quantification validated by HPLC-UV. Sarcosine levels were significantly higher in tumor cells, with recoveries between 90% and 102%. These results confirm the robustness and potential of MIP for the selective detection of sarcosine in rapid diagnostic strategies.
